title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.en: Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
units.literal: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
units.idiomatic: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

units.zh: 惠帝乃止。
units.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

units.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
units.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
units.idiomatic: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

units.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
units.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

units.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
units.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
units.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

units.zh: 由是奇之。
units.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
units.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

units.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
units.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
units.idiomatic: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

units.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
units.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
units.idiomatic: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

units.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
units.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
units.idiomatic: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

units.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
units.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
units.idiomatic: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

units.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
units.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
units.idiomatic: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

units.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
units.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.
units.idiomatic: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.

units.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
units.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.
units.idiomatic: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.

units.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
units.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
units.idiomatic: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

units.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
units.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.
units.idiomatic: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.

units.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
units.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

units.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
units.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
units.idiomatic: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

units.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
units.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.
units.idiomatic: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.

units.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
units.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.
units.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.

units.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
units.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.
units.idiomatic: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.

title.en: Volume 20 Treatises 10: Rites Part Two
title.raw: 卷二十 志第十 禮中 Volume 20 Treatises 10: Rites Part Two

units.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。
units.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the realm observed mourning for three days only.
units.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao died, the whole state wore mourning for three days and no more.

units.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。
units.literal: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent: once the burial ended he set aside formal mourning, yet still wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich food from his table.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Sima Yan kept the Han–Wei rule of ending court mourning at burial, but he still dressed in plain hemp deep robes, set aside brocade cushions, and ate only coarse fare.

units.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞夏商周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。
units.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.
units.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.

title.zh: 卷五十八 公孫弘卜式兒寬傳
title.en: Volume 58: Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi and Er Kuan
title.raw: 卷五十八 公孫弘卜式兒寬傳 Volume 58: Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi and Er Kuan

units.zh: 至洛陽，聞兒寬為之，褚大笑。
units.literal: When he reached Luoyang he heard that Er Kuan held it, and Chu burst out laughing.
units.idiomatic: At Luoyang he learned Er Kuan held the post—and laughed aloud.

units.zh: 及至，與寬議封禪於上前，大不能及，退而服曰：「上誠知人。」
units.literal: When he arrived and with Kuan debated feng and shan before the emperor, he could not match him; withdrawing he submitted, saying, "The sovereign truly knows men."
units.idiomatic: When Chu Da reached court and debated the Feng and Shan sacrifices with Kuan before the emperor, he could not match him. Afterward he conceded, "The sovereign truly knows men."

units.zh: 寬為御史大夫，以稱意任職，故久無有所匡諫於上，官屬易之。
units.literal: Kuan as imperial counselor, because he pleased the emperor in office, for long remonstrated on nothing to the emperor; his subordinates looked down on him.
units.idiomatic: Kuan pleased the emperor so well that he rarely criticized policy; his staff despised him for it.

units.zh: 居位九歲，以官卒。
units.literal: He occupied the post nine years and died in office.
units.idiomatic: Nine years he held the censorate, then died in harness.

units.zh: 是時，漢興六十餘載，海內艾安，府庫充實，而四夷未賓，制度多闕。
units.literal: At that time, more than sixty years after Han's rise, within the seas were at peace, granaries and treasuries were full, yet the four barbarians had not submitted and institutions were still largely lacking.
units.idiomatic: By then Han had stood sixty years at peace, the vaults were full, but the border tribes still stood outside the rites and many statutes waited to be written.

units.zh: 上方欲用文武，求之如弗及，始以蒲輪迎枚生，見主父而歎息。
units.literal: The emperor above wished to employ both civil and martial means and sought men as if he could not catch up; he first welcomed Master Mei with the rush-wheeled carriage and sighed on seeing Zhufu.
units.idiomatic: The sovereign meant to wield both wen and wu and hunted talent as if starved for it—he fetched Mei Sheng with the rush-wheeled cart and caught his breath at the sight of Zhufu Yan.

units.zh: 群士慕向，異人並出。
units.literal: The host of gentlemen yearned toward him; unusual men appeared together.
units.idiomatic: Scholars flocked to the capital; strange gifts turned up in pairs.

title.en: Volume 69 Biographies 19: Hou Junji, Zhang Liang, Xue Wanche
title.raw: 卷六十九 列傳第十九: 侯君集 張亮 薛萬徹 Volume 69 Biographies 19: Hou Junji, Zhang Liang, Xue Wanche

units.zh: 浚上表曰：「今年平吳，誠為大慶，於臣之身，更為咎累。」
units.literal: Jun submitted a memorial saying: "This year the pacification of Wu is truly a great celebration, but for your servant's person it is instead a burden of blame."
units.idiomatic: Jun wrote, "The conquest of Wu this year is a great celebration for the realm—but for me it has become a source of blame."

units.zh: 武帝赦而不推，拜輔國大將軍，封襄陽侯，賜絹萬匹。
units.literal: Emperor Wu pardoned him and did not pursue the matter, appointing him Supporting-the-State Grand General, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Xiangyang, and bestowing ten thousand bolts of silk.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu pardoned him without further inquiry, made him Supporting-the-State Grand General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xiangyang, and gave him ten thousand bolts of silk.

units.zh: 近隋新義郡公韓擒虎平陳之日，縱士卒暴亂叔寶宮內，文帝亦不問罪，雖不進爵，拜擒虎上柱國，賜物八千段。
units.literal: Recently, when Sui's Duke of Xinyi Han Qinhu pacified Chen, he let his soldiers run riot in Chen Shubao's palace; Emperor Wen also did not inquire into guilt—though he did not advance his rank, he made Qinhu Supreme Pillar of State and bestowed eight thousand lengths of goods.
units.idiomatic: More recently, when Sui's Duke of Xinyi Han Qinhu took Chen, his men looted Chen Shubao's palace. Emperor Wen did not prosecute him either. He did not raise his rank, but made Qinhu Supreme Pillar of State and gave him eight thousand lengths of goods.

title.raw: 卷二四 列傳第十六 孫搴 陳元康 杜弼 Volume 24 Biographies 16: Sun Qian (Eastern Wei); Chen Yuankang; Du Bi

units.zh: 武平末，國子祭酒，領尚書左丞。
units.literal: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the Imperial University and concurrently held the post of left vice director in the Masters of Writing.
units.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the imperial university and concurrently left vice director in the masters of writing.

units.zh: 周武帝平齊，命尚書左僕射陽休之以下知名朝士十八人隨駕入關，蕤兄弟並不預此名。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, downward to follow the imperial train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not among those named.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, left vice director of the masters of writing, downward to follow the train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not on the list.

units.zh: 臺卿後雖被徵，為其聾疾放歸。
units.literal: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.
units.idiomatic: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.

title.zh: 卷十二 王劉張李彭盧列傳
title.en: Volume 12: Biographies of Wang, Liu, Zhang, Li, Peng, Lu
title.raw: 卷十二 王劉張李彭盧列傳 Volume 12: Biographies of Wang, Liu, Zhang, Li, Peng, Lu

units.zh: 《續漢志》曰三水縣有左右谷，故城在今涇州安定縣南。
units.literal: The Treatise of the Continued Han says that Sanshui County had a Left Valley and a Right Valley; its old city lay south of present-day Anding County in Jingzhou.
units.idiomatic: The Treatise of the Continued Han says that Sanshui County had a Left Valley and a Right Valley; its old city lay south of present-day Anding County in Jingzhou.

units.zh: 王莽時，天下咸思漢德，芳由是詐自稱武帝曾孫劉文伯。
units.literal: In Wang Mang's time, all under heaven longed for Han virtue; Fang on this account falsely styled himself Emperor Wu's great-grandson Liu Wenbo.
units.idiomatic: While Wang Mang held the realm, men everywhere missed the virtue of Han; Lu Fang therefore passed himself off as Liu Wenbo, a great-grandson of Emperor Wu.

units.zh: 曾祖母匈奴谷蠡渾邪王之姊為武帝皇后，生三子。
units.literal: His great-grandmother was the Xiongnu Guili Hunye King's elder sister who became Emperor Wu's empress; she bore three sons.
units.idiomatic: His alleged great-grandmother was the sister of the Xiongnu prince Hunye of the Guili rank, who became Emperor Wu’s empress and bore three sons.

units.zh: 遭江充之亂，太子誅，皇后坐死，中子次卿亡之長陵，小子回卿逃於左谷。
units.literal: They suffered Jiang Chong's turmoil; the heir was executed; the empress died by implication; the middle son Ciqing fled to Changling; the youngest son Huiqing fled to Zuogu.
units.idiomatic: When Jiang Chong’s intrigue struck down the heir, the empress died with him; the middle son, Ciqing, fled to Changling and the youngest, Huiqing, to the Zuogu valley.

title.en: Volume 23 Han Records 15
title.raw: 卷23 漢紀十五

units.zh: 大雨，至於十月，渭橋絕。
units.literal: Heavy rain lasted until the tenth month; the Wei River bridge was cut off.
units.idiomatic: Heavy rain lasted until the tenth month; the Wei River bridge was washed out.

units.zh: 武帝初崩，賜諸侯王璽書。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu first died, imperial-seal letters of appointment were bestowed on the feudal kings.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu first died, imperial-seal letters of appointment were sent to the feudal kings.

units.zh: 燕王旦得書不肯哭，曰：「璽書封小，京師疑有變。」
units.literal: The Prince of Yan, Dan, received the letter and refused to mourn, saying: "The seal on the letter is small; the capital suspects there has been a change."
units.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Yan received the letter and refused to mourn, saying, "The seal on the letter is small—the capital may suspect something has changed."

units.zh: 及有詔褒賜旦錢三十萬，益封萬三千戶，旦怒曰：「我當為帝，何賜也！」
units.literal: When an edict came praising and rewarding Dan with three hundred thousand cash and an additional enfeoffment of thirteen thousand households, Dan angrily said: "I ought to be emperor—what is this reward!"
units.idiomatic: When an edict came praising and rewarding Dan with three hundred thousand cash and an additional enfeoffment of thirteen thousand households, Dan raged, "I ought to be emperor—what is this reward!"

units.zh: 遂與宗室中山哀王子長、齊孝王孫澤等結謀，詐言以武帝時受詔，得職吏事，修武備，備非常。
units.literal: He thereupon joined in conspiracy with the imperial clansman Chang, son of King Ai of Zhongshan, Sun Ze, grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others, falsely claiming that in Emperor Wu's time he had received an edict empowering him to manage officials and affairs, repair armaments, and guard against the unexpected.
units.idiomatic: He thereupon conspired with the imperial clansman Chang, son of King Ai of Zhongshan, Sun Ze, grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others, falsely claiming that in Emperor Wu's time he had received an edict empowering him to manage officials, repair armaments, and guard against the unexpected.

units.zh: 郎中成軫謂旦曰：「大王失職，獨可起而索，不可坐而得也。
units.literal: Palace Gentleman Cheng Zhen said to Dan: "Your Highness has lost your post; you can only rise and demand it—you cannot sit and obtain it.
units.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Cheng Zhen told Dan, "Your Highness has lost your place; you can only rise and demand it—you cannot sit and obtain it.

units.zh: 大王壹起，國中雖女子皆奮臂隨大王。」
units.literal: If Your Highness rises once, throughout the state even women will swing their arms and follow Your Highness."
units.idiomatic: If Your Highness rises once, throughout the state even women will take up arms and follow you."

units.zh: 旦即與澤謀，為奸書，言：「少帝非武帝子，大臣所共立；
units.literal: Dan at once plotted with Ze and forged a wicked letter, saying: "The young emperor is not Emperor Wu's son; the great ministers jointly established him;
units.idiomatic: Dan at once plotted with Ze and forged a seditious letter, saying, "The young emperor is not Emperor Wu's son; the great ministers jointly established him;

units.zh: 天下宜共伐之！」
units.literal: all under Heaven ought jointly to attack him!"
units.idiomatic: all under Heaven ought jointly to attack him!"

units.zh: 九月，丙子，秺敬侯金日磾薨。
units.literal: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Marquis Jing of Di Jin Midi died.
units.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Marquis Jing of Di Jin Midi died.

units.zh: 初，武帝病，有遺詔，封金日磾為秺侯，上官桀為安陽侯，霍光為博陸侯；
units.literal: At the outset, when Emperor Wu was ill, there was a testamentary edict enfeoffing Jin Midi as Marquis of Di, Shangguan Jie as Marquis of Anyang, and Huo Guang as Marquis of Bolu;
units.idiomatic: At the outset, when Emperor Wu was ill, a testamentary edict enfeoffed Jin Midi as Marquis of Di, Shangguan Jie as Marquis of Anyang, and Huo Guang as Marquis of Bolu;

units.zh: 皆以前捕反者馬何羅等功封。
units.literal: all were enfeoffed for their former merit in capturing the rebel Ma Heluo and others.
units.idiomatic: all were enfeoffed for their former merit in capturing the rebel Ma Heluo and others.

units.zh: 秋，八月，詔曰：「往年災害多，今年蠶、麥傷，所振貸種、食勿收責，毋令民出今年田租。」
units.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, an edict said: "In former years disasters were many; this year silkworms and wheat were harmed. The seed and food that were relieved and lent—do not collect repayment; do not make the people pay this year's field tax."
units.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, an edict said, "Disasters were many in former years; this year silkworms and wheat were harmed. Do not collect repayment for the seed and food that were relieved and lent; do not make the people pay this year's field tax."

units.zh: 初，武帝征伐匈奴，深入窮追，二十餘年，匈奴馬畜孕重墮殰，罷極，苦之。
units.literal: At the outset, Emperor Wu campaigned against the Xiongnu, driving deep in relentless pursuit for more than twenty years; the Xiongnu's horses and livestock, pregnant and heavy, miscarried and perished; exhausted to the limit, they suffered bitterly.
units.idiomatic: At the outset Emperor Wu campaigned against the Xiongnu, driving deep in relentless pursuit for more than twenty years; Xiongnu horses and livestock, pregnant and heavy, miscarried and perished; exhausted to the limit, they suffered bitterly.

units.zh: 常有欲和親意，未能得。
units.literal: They often had the intent to seek heqin peace but could not achieve it.
units.idiomatic: They often wished for heqin peace but could not achieve it.

units.zh: 王莽建羲和，考律呂，非不精也，不能救漸台之禍。
units.literal: Wang Mang established the Xihe office and examined pitch pipes—not that it was not precise, yet he could not avert the disaster of Jiantai.
units.idiomatic: Wang Mang established the Xihe office and tested the pitch pipes—not that this was not meticulous, yet he could not avert the disaster at Jiantai.

units.zh: 晉武制笛尺，調金石，非不詳也，不能弭平陽之災。
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin made the flute measure and tuned bells and stones—not that it was not thorough, yet he could not quell the calamity at Pingyang.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin fashioned the flute measure and tuned bells and stones—not that this was not exhaustive, yet he could not quell the calamity at Pingyang.

units.zh: 梁武帝立四器、調八音，非不察也，不能免台城之辱。
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang established the four instruments and tuned the eight tones—not that it was not discriminating, yet he could not escape the humiliation of Tai Cheng.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang established the four pitch standards and tuned the eight tones—not that this was not discerning, yet he could not escape the humiliation at Tai Cheng.

units.zh: 武帝異其文，拜軍為謁者給事中。
units.literal: Emperor Wu marveled at his writing and appointed Jun Herald and Palace Attendant.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was struck by the quality of his prose and named him court herald with standing access to the inner palace.

units.zh: 從上幸雍祠五畤，獲白麟，一角而五蹄。
units.literal: He followed the emperor in visiting Yong to sacrifice at the five altars; they obtained a white unicorn, one horn and five hoofs.
units.idiomatic: He accompanied the sovereign to Yong for the sacrifices at the five shrines, where hunters brought in a white unicorn bearing a single horn and five hooves.

units.zh: 時又得奇木，其枝旁出，輒復合於木上。
units.literal: At the same time they also obtained a strange tree; its branches came out sideways and then again joined together on the tree.
units.idiomatic: About the same time someone presented a freakish tree whose limbs jutted sideways only to fuse back into the trunk.

units.zh: 上異此二物，博謀群臣。
units.literal: The emperor marveled at these two things and broadly consulted the ministers.
units.idiomatic: The emperor regarded both prodigies as extraordinary and asked his officials for wide-ranging counsel.

units.zh: 軍上對曰：
units.literal: Jun submitted a reply, saying:
units.idiomatic: Zhong Jun responded with a memorial that read:

units.zh: 故周至成王，然後制定，而休徵之應見。
units.literal: Therefore Zhou reached King Cheng, and afterward regulations were fixed, and the response of auspicious signs appeared.
units.idiomatic: The house of Zhou did not complete its statutes until the reign of King Cheng; only then did propitious omens begin to answer its virtue.

units.zh: 陛下盛日月之光，垂聖思於勒成，專神明之敬，奉燔瘞於郊宮，獻享之精交神，積和之氣塞明，而異獸來獲，宜矣。
units.literal: Your Majesty flourishes the light of sun and moon, hangs sagely thought on carved completion, devotes reverence to spirits, offers burning and burying at the suburban palace; the essence of offerings and feasting intersects spirits, accumulated harmony qi fills brightness, and strange beasts come to be captured—it is fitting.
units.idiomatic: Your Majesty outshines sun and moon, bends sage reflection toward perfecting the record, concentrates reverence on the gods, and presents burnt and buried offerings at the suburban shrines until the subtle ether of sacrifice mingles with the spirits and a tide of harmony fills the bright sky. Small wonder strange beasts should present themselves.

units.zh: 昔武王中流未濟，白魚入於王舟，俯取以燎，群公咸曰「休哉！」
units.literal: Formerly King Wu, midstream not yet crossed, a white fish entered the king's boat; he bent and took it to burn as offering; the dukes all said, 'Auspicious!'
units.idiomatic: Once, when King Wu had not yet finished fording the river, a white fish leaped into his barge; he lifted it out for a burnt offering, and the nobles cried, 'Excellent omen!'

units.zh: 斯拱而俟之耳！
units.literal: This is folding hands and awaiting it!
units.idiomatic: You have only to fold your hands and wait.

units.zh: 對奏，上甚異之，由是改元為元狩。
units.literal: When the reply was presented, the emperor greatly marveled at it; thereby the era name was changed to Yuanshou.
units.idiomatic: The emperor was so struck by the memorial that he renamed the reign Yuanshou.

units.zh: 後數月，越地及匈奴名王有率眾來降者，時皆以軍言為中。
units.literal: Several months later, in Yue territory and among the Xiongnu famous kings there were those who led crowds to come surrender; at the time all took Jun's words as hitting the mark.
units.idiomatic: Within a few months Yue chiefs and noted Xiongnu princes began leading their followers in to surrender—just as Zhong Jun had predicted.

units.zh: 奏可。
units.literal: The memorial was approved.
units.idiomatic: The throne approved the memorial.

units.zh: 上善其詰，有詔示御史大夫。
units.literal: The emperor praised his examination; there was an edict shown to the Imperial Counselor.
units.idiomatic: The emperor commended Zhong Jun's cross-examination and issued an edict laying out the case for the Imperial Counselor.

units.zh: 初，軍從濟南當詣博士，步入關，關吏予軍繻。
units.literal: At first, when Jun was going from Jinan to attend the erudites, he walked into the pass; the pass clerk gave Jun a silk tally.
units.idiomatic: Long ago, when Zhong Jun left Jinan to enroll as a student of the imperial academy, he entered the frontier pass on foot, and the gate officer handed him the return-token of split silk.

units.zh: 太康初為博士，會議齊王攸之國，加崇典禮，暾與諸博士坐議迕旨。
units.literal: At the beginning of Taikang he became erudite; when they convened on Prince of Qi You's fief—raising ceremonial honors—Tun with the other erudites sat debating and offended the intent.
units.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he served as erudite; debating Prince You's investiture he challenged imperial policy with his colleagues.

units.zh: 武帝大怒，收暾等付廷尉。
units.literal: Emperor Wu was greatly angry—seized Tun and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu jailed Tun and the classicists in the ministry of justice.

units.zh: 會赦得出，免官。
units.literal: When an amnesty occurred they obtained release—removed from office.
units.idiomatic: An amnesty freed him but stripped his post.

units.zh: 毅奏中護軍羊琇犯憲應死。
units.literal: Yi memorialized that Commander Who Guards the Army Yang Xiu violated statute—deserved death.
units.idiomatic: Yi impeached Yang Xiu for breaking the law—a capital crime.

units.zh: 武帝與琇有舊，乃遣齊王攸喻毅，毅許之。
units.literal: Emperor Wu had old ties with Xiu—sent Prince of Qi You to persuade Yi—Yi assented.
units.idiomatic: The emperor, owing Yang Xiu a favor, had Prince You sway Yi—Yi relented.

units.zh: 衛正色以為不可，逕自馳車入護軍營，收琇屬吏，考問陰私，先奏琇所犯狼藉，然後言於毅。
units.literal: Wei with stern color held it impossible—went straight driving carriage into the guards' camp—seized Xiu's subordinate clerks—examined hidden affairs—first memorialized Xiu's crimes in disorder—then reported to Yi.
units.idiomatic: Cheng Wei refused, galloped into the guard camp, seized Yang Xiu’s staff, unearthed his secrets, and first reported the debacle to court—then told Yi.

units.zh: 奄有參墟，聲流無窮。
units.literal: He embraced the lands around Shen; his fame flows without end.
units.idiomatic: He held the heartland east of Shen; his fame knows no end.

units.zh: 歌武帝曹毗
units.literal: Hymn to Emperor Wu (by Cao Pi)
units.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Wu — Cao Pi

units.zh: 于穆武皇，允龔欽明。
units.literal: Oh, august Martial Sovereign—truly reverent, truly luminous.
units.idiomatic: Oh, august Martial Sovereign—supremely reverent, supremely bright.

units.zh: 應期登禪，龍飛紫庭。
units.literal: At the appointed season he ascended the abdication throne; the dragon flew within the purple court.
units.idiomatic: When the hour came he mounted the abdicated throne; the dragon soared within the purple precincts.

units.zh: 故有大火。
units.literal: Therefore there was the great fire.
units.idiomatic: Hence the great conflagration.

units.zh: 晉武帝太康八年三月乙丑，震災西閣、楚王所止坊，及臨商觀牕。
units.literal: On the yichou day of the third month of the eighth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, lightning struck the western gallery, the ward where the Prince of Chu resided, and the windows of the Linshang Observatory.
units.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the third month of the eighth Taikang year under Emperor Wu of Jin, lightning struck the western gallery, the Prince of Chu's residential ward, and the windows of the Linshang Observatory.

units.zh: 十年四月癸丑，崇賢殿災。
units.literal: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year, the Chongxian Hall burned.
units.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year fire destroyed the Chongxian Hall.

units.zh: 其高皇、太皇、外處君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
units.literal: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.
units.idiomatic: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.

units.zh: 晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。
units.literal: Sima Yi founded Jin's enterprise, so when Emperor Wu received the mandate, Emperor Xuan likewise became Grand Ancestor.

units.zh: 其征西、豫章、潁川、京兆府君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
units.literal: The Zhengxi, Yuzhang, Yingchuan, Jingzhao, and other lords were honored as kin and excluded from the zhao-mu shared offerings.

units.zh: 二年，復為都官尚書。
units.literal: In the second year he again became Minister of the Ministry of Justice.
units.idiomatic: The following year he was again appointed Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 侯景反，攻陷曆陽，帝問侃討景之策。
units.literal: Hou Jing rebelled, captured Liyang, and the emperor asked Kan for a strategy to suppress Jing.
units.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled and took Liyang, the emperor asked Kan how best to destroy him.

units.zh: 侃求以二千人急據採石，令邵陵王襲取壽春，使景進不得前，退失巢窟，烏合之眾，自然瓦解。
units.literal: Kan requested two thousand men to seize Caishi in haste, and ordered the Prince of Shaoling to strike and take Shouchun, so that Jing advancing could not proceed and retreating would lose his nest — the mob gathered at random would naturally disintegrate.
units.idiomatic: Kan asked for two thousand men to seize Caishi immediately and urged the Prince of Shaoling to take Shouchun by surprise, so Hou Jing could neither advance nor retreat to a secure base; his ragtag following would fall apart on its own.

units.zh: 朱異、張綰議出擊之。
units.literal: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan debated sallying out to strike them.
units.idiomatic: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan urged a sortie against the encirclement.

units.zh: 帝以問侃，侃曰：「不可，賊多日攻城，既不能下，故立長圍，欲引城中降者耳。
units.literal: The emperor questioned Kan; Kan said: "It cannot be done. The rebels have besieged for many days and could not take the city, so they establish a long encirclement intending only to lure those in the city who would surrender.
units.idiomatic: The emperor asked Kan's view. Kan said, "No. They have failed to take the city by assault, so they are building a long siege line to tempt defectors inside the walls — that is all.

units.zh: 今擊之，出人若少，不足破賊；
units.literal: If we strike now and send out few men, it is insufficient to break the rebels;
units.idiomatic: If we sortie with too few men, we won't break them;

units.zh: 褒曆事三帝，以忠厚見知。
units.literal: Bao served through three emperors and was known for loyalty and honesty.
units.idiomatic: Bao served three emperors and was esteemed for his loyalty and integrity.

units.zh: 武帝深相敬重，常以師道處之，每入朝見，必有詔令坐，然始論政事。
units.literal: Emperor Wu deeply respected him, constantly treating him with the ceremony due a teacher; each time he entered court for audience there was always an edict ordering him to be seated before political matters were discussed.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu held him in the highest regard and always treated him as a teacher. Whenever Bao came to court, the emperor would order him seated before any business was discussed.

units.zh: 卒，贈涇、岐、燕三州刺史，諡曰貞。
units.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the three provincial governorships of Jing, Qi, and Yan; his posthumous name was Zhen.
units.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously honored with the titles of governor of Jing, Qi, and Yan provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).

units.zh: 年十二，朗薨，后哀戚哭泣，發于自然，其父益加敬異。
units.literal: At twelve Lang died; the empress mourned and wept in grief, arising from the natural; her father increasingly respected her as unusual.
units.idiomatic: When Wang Lang died she was twelve; her grief was utterly spontaneous, and her father prized her even more.

units.zh: 既笄，歸于文帝，生武帝及遼東悼王定國、齊獻王攸、城陽哀王兆、廣漢殤王廣德、京兆公主。
units.literal: After capping-age she married Emperor Wen and bore Emperor Wu, Prince Dingguo of Liaodong, Prince You of Qi, Prince Zhao of Chengyang, Prince Guangde of Guanghan, and the Princess of Jingzhao.
units.idiomatic: After coming of age she married Sima Zhao (later Emperor Wen) and bore Sima Yan (Emperor Wu), Princes Dingguo, You, Zhao, and Guangde, and the Princess of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 后事舅姑盡婦道，謙沖接下，嬪御有序。
units.literal: The empress served parents-in-law exhausting wife’s way, humble and yielding in receiving those below, concubines and attendants having order.
units.idiomatic: She observed every duty to her in-laws, treated inferiors with modesty, and kept the inner household in harmony.

units.zh: 會後果反。
units.literal: Hui afterward indeed rebelled.
units.idiomatic: Zhong Hui later rose in rebellion, just as she foretold.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，尊為皇太后，宮曰崇化。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she was honored as empress dowager; the palace was called Chonghua.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne she became empress dowager, with residence in Chonghua Palace.

units.zh: 初置宮卿，重選其職，以太常諸葛緒為衛尉，太僕劉原為太僕，宗正曹楷為少府。
units.literal: At first palace ministers were installed; their offices were heavily selected—Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhuge Xu as Commandant of the Guard, Grand Coachman Liu Yuan as Grand Coachman, Director of the Imperial Clan Cao Kai as Privy Treasurer.
units.idiomatic: She established palace ministries with careful appointments: Zhuge Xu as minister of the guard, Liu Yuan as grand coachman, Cao Kai as privy treasurer.

units.zh: 而敦睦九族，垂心萬物，言必典禮，浸潤不行。
units.literal: Yet she treated the nine kindreds warmly, let her heart hang over all things; speech always followed canon and ritual; seeping influence did not proceed.
units.idiomatic: She cherished every branch of kin, cared for all living things, spoke only in classical idiom, and never let private bias seep into policy.

units.zh: 帝以后母羊氏未崇諡號，泰始三年下詔曰：「昔漢文追崇靈文之號，武、宣有平原、博平之封，咸所以奉尊尊之敬，廣親親之恩也。
units.literal: The emperor because the empress’s mother the Yang clan had not been honored with posthumous title, in the third Taishi year issued an edict saying: “Formerly Han Wen posthumously elevated the title of Lingwen; Wu and Xuan had enfeoffments of Pingyuan and Boping—all were means to serve respect to the honored and widen kindness to kin.
units.idiomatic: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi conferred the posthumous title Lingwen; Emperors Wu and Xuan of Han granted the fiefs of Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.

units.zh: 故衛將軍、蘭陵景侯夫人羊氏，含章體順，仁德醇備，內承世冑，出嬪大國，三從之行，率禮無違。
units.literal: Therefore Lady Yang, wife of General Who Guards the Army, Marquis Jing of Lanling, contained pattern and embodied compliance; humane virtue pure and complete; inwardly inheriting generations of lineage, outwardly marrying a great state; in the conduct of the three followings, leading ritual without violation.
units.idiomatic: Lady Yang, widow of Wang Su, the General Who Guards the Army and Marquis Jing of Lanling, bore inward grace and outward modesty, fulfilled every womanly virtue, linked great houses by marriage, and observed the three obediences without fault.

units.zh: 四年，后崩，時年五十二，合葬崇陽陵。
units.literal: In the fourth year the empress died. She was fifty-two at death and was buried jointly at Chongyang Mausoleum.
units.idiomatic: In the fourth year she died at fifty-two and was laid beside him in Chongyang Mausoleum.

units.zh: 將遷祔，帝手疏后德行，命史官為哀策曰：
units.literal: When she was to be moved for joint burial, the emperor personally drafted an account of her conduct and ordered the historiographers to compose a dirge of lament, saying:
units.idiomatic: When her cortège was readied for burial at his side, he drafted her virtues in his own hand and told the historiographers to write a lament—thus:

units.zh: 明明先后，興我晉道。
units.literal: O clear-bright late queen, you raised our Jin way.
units.idiomatic: Radiant queen who went before, you lifted high our Jin house.

units.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
units.literal: Alas, oh grief!
units.idiomatic: Alas for this sorrow!

units.zh: 其後帝追慕不已，復下詔曰：「外曾祖母故司徒王朗夫人楊氏，舅氏尊屬，鄭、劉二從母，先后至愛。
units.literal: Afterward the emperor’s longing did not cease; he again issued an edict saying: “My maternal great-grandmother, Lady Yang, wife of former Minister of Education Wang Lang, my uncles’ honored kin, and my two maternal aunts of the Zheng and Liu clans were deeply beloved by the late consorts.
units.idiomatic: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were dearly loved by the late empress.

units.zh: 每惟聖善，敦睦遺旨，渭陽之感，永懷靡及。
units.literal: Whenever pondering their sacred goodness and generous instructions, the Wei-yang longing—forever cherished yet never attained.
units.idiomatic: Whenever I recall their kindness and the generous instructions they left, the ache of a nephew for his mother’s kin stays with me yet can never be satisfied.

title.en: Volume 60a: Biography of Ma Rong
title.raw: 卷六十上 馬融列傳 Volume 60a: Biography of Ma Rong

units.zh: 颸，疾風也，音楚疑也。
units.literal: Si is swift wind; pronunciation chu-yi.
units.idiomatic: Si names slick breezes.

units.zh: 武帝秋風詞曰：「蕭鼓鳴兮發棹歌。」
units.literal: Emperor Wu's Autumn Wind Song says: "Flutes and drums sound; the oar song begins."
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's Autumn Wind Song says: "Flutes and drums sound; the oar song begins."

units.zh: 劉向列女傳曰：「津更之女，中流奏河激之歌。」
units.literal: Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women says: "The ferryman's daughter performed the song "River Surge" in midstream."
units.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women says: "The ferryman's daughter performed the song "River Surge" in midstream."

title.zh: 卷二十八 志第十八 五行中
title.en: Volume 28 Treatises 18: Five Elements Part Two
title.raw: 卷二十八 志第十八 五行中 Volume 28 Treatises 18: Five Elements Part Two

units.zh: 或曰孫休見立之祥也。
units.literal: Others say it signified Sun Xiu's enthronement.
units.idiomatic: Another reading favored Sun Xiu.

units.zh: 武帝太康十年，洛陽宮西宜秋裏石生地中，始高三尺，如香鈩形，後如傴人，槃薄不可掘。
units.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 10 — west of the Luoyang palace, in Yiqiu ward, a stone grew out of the ground; at first it was three chi high and shaped like an incense burner, later like a bent-over man, spreading thickly and impossible to dig out.
units.idiomatic: In Taikang 10 under Emperor Wu, a stone sprouted in Yiqiu ward west of the Luoyang palace, changing from an incense-burner shape into something like a hunched man.

units.zh: 案劉向說，此白眚也。
units.literal: Liu Xiang's doctrine calls this white ill-omen.
units.idiomatic: Liu Xiang filed it under white shang.

units.zh: 明年宮車晏駕，王室始騷，卒以亂亡。
units.literal: Next year the imperial carriage halted; the royal house first stirred and ended in chaos.
units.idiomatic: Sima Yan died; turmoil followed.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「石立如人，庶士為天下雄。」
units.literal: Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man — commoners become heroes under heaven."
units.idiomatic: Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man — commoners become heroes under heaven."

units.zh: 是後騰為汲桑所殺，而天下遂亂。
units.literal: Afterward Teng was killed by Ji Sang and the realm slid into chaos.
units.idiomatic: Ji Sang slew him; anarchy spread.

units.zh: 武帝泰始八年五月，蜀地雨白毛，此白祥也。
units.literal: Emperor Wu, Taishi 8, fifth month — white hair rained down in Shu; this was a white omen.
units.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, white hair fell like rain in Shu, a white omen.

units.zh: 時益州刺史皇甫晏伐汶山胡，從事何旅固諫，不從，牙門張弘等困眾之怨，誣晏謀逆，害之。
units.literal: Then Inspector Huangfu Yan campaigned against Wenshan Hu; aide He Lu counseled against it; ignored; gate officer Zhang Hong exploited troop hatred, slandered Yan as rebel, murdered him.
units.idiomatic: Huangfu Yan's western war brought mutiny and death.

title.en: Volume 30 Treatises 20: Punishment and Law
title.raw: 卷三十 志第二十 刑法 Volume 30 Treatises 20: Punishment and Law

units.zh: 泰始三年，事畢，表上。
units.literal: In Taishi third year the work finished and they memorialized it upward.
units.idiomatic: the third year of Taishi (267 CE) saw the finished code presented to the throne.

units.zh: 武帝詔曰：「昔蕭何以定律令受封，叔孫通制儀為奉常，賜金五百斤，弟子百人皆為郎。
units.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict, saying, "Formerly Xiao He received an enfeoffment for settling statutes and ordinances, and Shusun Tong made ritual regulations, became Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was granted five hundred jin of gold, and one hundred of his disciples all became gentlemen.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu issued an edict, saying, "Formerly Xiao He received an enfeoffment for settling statutes and ordinances, and Shusun Tong made ritual regulations, became Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was granted five hundred jin of gold, and one hundred of his disciples all became gentlemen.

units.zh: 夫立功立事，古今之所重，宜加祿賞，其詳考差敘。
units.literal: Establishing merit has always mattered—add salaries and rewards; investigate ranks carefully.
units.idiomatic: Reward the compilers commensurate with their service.

units.zh: 輒如詔簡異弟子百人，隨才品用，賞帛萬餘匹。」
units.literal: At once, according to the edict, one hundred exceptional disciples were selected, employed according to their talents and grades, and rewarded with more than ten thousand bolts of silk."
units.idiomatic: At once, according to the edict, one hundred exceptional disciples were selected, employed according to their talents and grades, and rewarded with more than ten thousand bolts of silk."

units.zh: 武帝親自臨講，使裴楷執讀。
units.literal: Emperor Wu personally attended the lecture and had Pei Kai read aloud.
units.idiomatic: Wudi presided while Pei Kai recited the new code.

units.zh: 四年正月，大赦天下，乃班新律。
units.literal: Fourth year, first month, he proclaimed a general amnesty and promulgated the new statutes.
units.idiomatic: In the first month of year four he amnestied the realm and published the Jin code.

title.en: Volume 26 Han Records 18
title.raw: 卷26 漢紀十八

units.zh: 春，正月，上始行幸甘泉，郊泰畤，三月，行幸河東，祠后土。
units.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor first undertook the journey to favor Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the Great Altar; in the third month he undertook the journey to favor Hedong and sacrificed to the Queen of Earth.
units.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor first traveled to Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the Great Altar; in the third month he traveled to Hedong and sacrificed to the Queen of Earth.

units.zh: 上頗修武帝故事，謹齋祀之禮，以方士言增置神祠；
units.literal: The emperor largely restored Emperor Wu's practices, carefully observing fasting and sacrificial rites; on the word of fangshi he added divine shrines;
units.idiomatic: The emperor largely revived Emperor Wu's ways, carefully observing fasting and sacrifice; on fangshi advice he added shrines;

units.zh: 聞益州有金馬、碧雞之神，可醮祭而致，於是遣諫大夫蜀郡王褒使持節而求之。
units.literal: hearing that in Yizhou were the spirits of the Golden Horse and Green Cock, whom libation-sacrifice could summon, he thereupon dispatched Remonstrance Grandee Wang Bao of Shu commandery as envoy bearing credentials to seek them.
units.idiomatic: hearing that Yizhou held the spirits of the Golden Horse and Green Cock, whom libation could summon, he dispatched Remonstrance Grandee Wang Bao of Shu as envoy bearing credentials to seek them.

title.zh: 卷一百〇一 載記第一 劉元海（劉淵） 劉宣
title.en: Volume 101 Records 1: Liu Yuanhai and Liu Xuan
title.raw: 卷一百〇一 載記第一 劉元海（劉淵） 劉宣 Volume 101 Records 1: Liu Yuanhai and Liu Xuan

units.zh: 咸熙中，為任子在洛陽，文帝深待之。
units.literal: In the Xianxi era he was hostage-son in Luoyang, and Emperor Wen treated him with deep favour.
units.idiomatic: During Xianxi he was a hostage noble in Luoyang, and Sima Zhao favoured him.

units.zh: 泰始之後，渾又屢言之于武帝。
units.literal: After Taishi, Hun again repeatedly spoke of him to Emperor Wu.
units.idiomatic: After Taishi began Wang Hun kept recommending him to Sima Yan.

units.zh: 帝召與語，大悅之，謂王濟曰：「劉元海容儀機鑒，雖由餘、日磾無以加也。」
units.literal: The Emperor summoned him to converse, greatly delighted in him, and said to Wang Ji, "Liu Yuanhai's mien and insight—even You Yu and Jin Midi could not surpass him."
units.idiomatic: The emperor interviewed Liu Yuan and told Wang Ji, "For presence and penetration even Jin Midi and You Yu would not surpass him."

units.zh: 濟對曰：「元海儀容機鑒，實如聖旨，然其文武才幹賢於二子遠矣。
units.literal: Ji replied, "Yuanhai's bearing and insight are indeed as Your Majesty's edict says, yet his civil and martial talent and capacity surpass those two sons by far.
units.idiomatic: Wang Ji answered, "You speak true of his charisma, but his civil and military gifts outstrip those two by far.

units.zh: 陛下若任之以東南之事，吳會不足平也。」
units.literal: If Your Majesty assigns him southeast affairs, Wu and Yue will not be enough to pacify."
units.idiomatic: Give him the southeast and Wu-Yue would fall in a campaign."

units.zh: 帝稱善。
units.literal: The Emperor praised it as good.
units.idiomatic: The emperor called it excellent advice.

units.zh: 孔恂、楊珧進曰：「臣觀元海之才，當今懼無其比，陛下若輕其眾，不足以成事；
units.literal: Kong Xun and Yang Yao advanced, saying, "Your servant observes Yuanhai's talent—today there is none to compare; if Your Majesty lightly employs his host, it will not suffice to accomplish the deed;
units.idiomatic: Kong Xun and Yang Yao objected: "No one today matches Liu Yuan; if you treat his tribes lightly you may fail the mission;

units.zh: 若舉天阻之固以資之，無乃不可乎！」
units.literal: To supply him with the solidity of heaven's barrier—can that be permissible!"
units.idiomatic: Hand him the northern bastions and you arm a dragon—how can that be wise?"

units.zh: 帝默然。
units.literal: The Emperor was silent.
units.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

units.zh: 後秦涼覆沒，帝疇咨將帥，上党李憙曰：「陛下誠能發匈奴五部之眾，假元海一將軍之號，鼓行而西，可指期而定。」
units.literal: Later Qin and Liang were overthrown; the Emperor consulted on commanders, and Li Xi of Shangdang said, "If Your Majesty truly can mobilize the five Xiongnu sections and lend Yuanhai a general's title, beating the drum westward, it can be settled on a set date."
units.idiomatic: When Liang collapsed the court debated generals; Li Xi of Shangdang said, "Mobilize the five Xiongnu divisions, give Liu Yuan a general's baton, and march west on schedule—the west will fall."

units.zh: 蛟龍得雲雨，非復池中物也。」
units.literal: When a flood-dragon gains clouds and rain, it is no longer a creature in the pond."
units.idiomatic: Give a kraken cloud and rain and it leaves the pool forever."

units.zh: 帝乃止。
units.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
units.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

units.zh: 後王彌從洛陽東歸，元海餞彌于九曲之濱。
units.literal: Later Wang Mi returned east from Luoyang; Yuanhai feasted Mi on the bank of the Jiuqu.
units.idiomatic: When Wang Mi left Luoyang for the east, Liu Yuan feasted him on the Jiuqu bend.

units.zh: 因慷慨歔欷，縱酒長嘯，聲調亮然，坐者為之流涕。
units.literal: Thereupon he was stirred and sighed, poured wine freely and gave a long whistle; the tone was clear and bright, and those seated wept for him.
units.idiomatic: He grew fierce with wine, whistled long and loud, and every guest wept at the sound.

units.zh: 齊王攸時在九曲，比聞而馳遣視之，見元海在焉，言於帝曰：「陛下不除劉元海，臣恐并州不得久寧。」
units.literal: Prince Sima You of Qi was at that time at Jiuqu; when he heard nearby he galloped to send someone to look, and seeing Yuanhai there, said to the Emperor, "If Your Majesty does not remove Liu Yuanhai, your servant fears Bingzhou will not long be tranquil."
units.idiomatic: Prince Sima You was nearby at Jiuqu; he rode over, found Liu Yuan at the banquet, and warned the emperor, "If you leave Liu Yuan alive, Bingzhou will not stay quiet."

units.zh: 王渾進曰：「元海長者，渾為君王保明之。
units.literal: Wang Hun advanced, saying, "Yuanhai is an elder; Hun for the prince-king vouches for him.
units.idiomatic: Wang Hun cut in: "Liu Yuan is a man of honour—I will answer for him before Your Majesty.

units.zh: 且大晉方表信殊俗，懷遠以德，如之何以無萌之疑殺人侍子，以示晉德不弘。」
units.literal: Moreover Great Jin is just now displaying trust toward alien customs, cherishing the distant by virtue—how can we, on suspicion without sprout, kill a man's attendant-son and thereby show that Jin's virtue is not broad."
units.idiomatic: The court is trying to win the frontier by trust; killing a blameless hostage on a whim would prove our virtue is narrow."

units.zh: 帝曰：「渾言是也。」
units.literal: The Emperor said, "Hun's words are right."
units.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Hun is correct."

units.zh: 會豹卒，以元海代為左部帥。
units.literal: When Bao died, Yuanhai was appointed in his stead as commander of the left section.
units.idiomatic: When Liu Bao died Liu Yuan succeeded him as left-section chief.

title.zh: 卷十四 志第四 地理上
title.en: Volume 14 Treatises 4: Geography Part One
title.raw: 卷十四 志第四 地理上 Volume 14 Treatises 4: Geography Part One

units.zh: 男邑四百戶，地方四十里。
units.literal: Barons' towns four hundred households, territory forty li square.
units.idiomatic: Baronial seats stopped at four hundred households on forty li square.

units.zh: [5]武帝泰始元年，封諸王以郡爲國。
units.literal: [5] In Jin Emperor Wu's first Taishi year, enfeoffed the various kings taking commanderies as states.
units.idiomatic: [5] In the first year of Taishi Emperor Wu made each prince's domain a full commandery-sized kingdom.

units.zh: 邑二萬戶爲大國，置上中下三軍，兵五千人；
units.literal: Towns twenty thousand households are a great state; establish upper, middle, and lower three armies—soldiers five thousand men;
units.idiomatic: Twenty thousand households marked a great kingdom with upper, middle, and lower armies totaling five thousand troops;

units.zh: 罷五等之制，公侯邑萬戶以上爲大國，五千戶以上爲次國，不滿五千戶爲小國。
units.literal: Abolished the five-rank system: dukes and marquises' towns ten thousand households and above are great states; five thousand households and above are next-rank states; not filling five thousand households are small states.
units.idiomatic: When the five-grade scheme was dropped, dukes and marquises above ten thousand households ranked as great fiefs, those above five thousand as middling, and the rest as small.

units.zh: 太康元年，平吳，大凡戶二百四十五萬九千八百四十，口一千六百一十六萬三千八百六十三。
units.literal: Taikang first year, pacified Wu; in all households two million four hundred fifty-nine thousand eight hundred forty, mouths sixteen million one hundred sixty-three thousand eight hundred sixty-three.
units.idiomatic: After Wu fell in the first Taikang year the census added 2,459,840 households and 16,163,863 mouths to the Jin totals.

units.zh: 而江左諸國並三分食一，元帝渡江，太興元年，始制九分食一。
units.literal: Moreover the various states east of the Jiang all together took one-third as food; Yuandi crossed the river; Taixing first year, first regulated one-ninth as food.
units.idiomatic: The various states east of the Jiang had all drawn one-third of their revenues as food-income; after Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi, in the first year of Taixing the court first set that princely share at one-ninth.

title.zh: 卷三十五 列傳第五 陳騫 裴秀
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 5: Chen Qian; Pei Xiu
title.raw: 卷三十五 列傳第五 陳騫 裴秀 Volume 35 Biographies 5: Chen Qian; Pei Xiu

units.zh: 楷善宣吐，左右屬目，聽者忘倦。
units.literal: Kai spoke with luminous clarity; attendants hung on every word and listeners forgot fatigue.
units.idiomatic: His exposition captivated the hall.

units.zh: 武帝為撫軍，妙選僚采，以楷為參軍事。
units.literal: While Emperor Wu still served as General Who Supports the Army, he chose Kai as military administrator.
units.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him staff adviser during the princely generalship.

units.zh: 吏部郎缺，文帝問其人於鍾會。
units.literal: The personnel director post stood empty; Emperor Wen asked Zhong Hui whom to appoint.
units.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked Zhong Hui who should head personnel.

units.zh: 轉中書郎，出入宮省，見者肅然改容。
units.literal: Transferred to palace secretariat gentleman, he passed through palace gates so strikingly that onlookers straightened their bearing.
units.idiomatic: Palace corridors fell silent when he passed.

units.zh: 武帝初登阼，探策以卜世數多少，而得一，帝不悅，群臣失色，莫有言者。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu first mounted the throne he drew oracle slips on dynastic longevity and drew "one"; the emperor frowned, ministers paled, none spoke.
units.idiomatic: An ill-omened slip "one" from the imperial divination silenced the court.

units.zh: 楷正容儀，和其聲氣，從容進曰：「臣聞天得一以清，地得一以甯，王侯得一以為天下貞。」
units.literal: Kai corrected his bearing, harmonized his voice and breath, and calmly advanced, saying, "I have heard that Heaven obtains the One and is clear, Earth obtains the One and is tranquil, and kings and lords obtain the One and become the rectitude of all under Heaven."
units.idiomatic: Kai corrected his bearing, harmonized his voice and breath, and calmly advanced, saying, "I have heard that Heaven obtains the One and is clear, Earth obtains the One and is tranquil, and kings and lords obtain the One and become the rectitude of all under Heaven."

units.zh: 武帝大悅，群臣皆稱萬歲。
units.literal: Emperor Wu rejoiced; everyone shouted long live the emperor.
units.idiomatic: The emperor brightened and the hall cheered.

units.zh: 俄拜散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、河內太守，入為屯騎校尉、右軍將軍，轉侍中。
units.literal: Soon he was supernumerary gentleman, then attendant, governor of Henei, colonel of household troops, general of the right guard, and palace attendant.
units.idiomatic: Promotions swept him through Henei, camp command, the right guard, and back to attendant.

units.zh: 安於毀譽，其行己任率，皆此類也。
units.literal: Untroubled by praise or blame, he lived candidly—always thus.
units.idiomatic: He shrugged at gossip and followed instinct.

units.zh: 與山濤、和嶠並以盛德居位，帝嘗問曰：「朕應天順時，海內更始，天下風聲，何得何失？」
units.literal: Together with Shan Tao and He Jiao, he held office with abundant virtue. The emperor once asked, "I respond to Heaven and follow the time, and within the seas there is a new beginning. In the voices of custom throughout the realm, what has been gained and what has been lost?"
units.idiomatic: Together with Shan Tao and He Jiao, he held office with abundant virtue. The emperor once asked, "I respond to Heaven and follow the time, and within the seas there is a new beginning. In the voices of custom throughout the realm, what has been gained and what has been lost?"

units.zh: 楷對曰：「陛下受命，四海承風，所以未比德於堯舜者，但以賈充之徒尚在朝耳。
units.literal: Kai replied, "Your Majesty has received the mandate, and the four seas follow your influence. The reason your virtue is not yet compared with Yao and Shun is only that the likes of Jia Chong are still at court.
units.idiomatic: Kai replied, "Your Majesty has received the mandate, and the four seas follow your influence. The reason your virtue is not yet compared with Yao and Shun is only that the likes of Jia Chong are still at court.

units.zh: 方宜引天下賢人，與弘正道，不宜示人以私。」
units.literal: Just now you should draw in worthy men from all under Heaven and with them broaden the correct Way; you should not show people private favor."
units.idiomatic: Just now you should draw in worthy men from all under Heaven and with them broaden the correct Way; you should not show people private favor."

units.zh: 時任愷、庾純亦以充為言，帝乃出充為關中都督。
units.literal: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him; the emperor posted Chong to frontier command.
units.idiomatic: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him until the emperor reassigned Chong as Guanzhong area commander.

units.zh: 充納女于太子，乃止。
units.literal: Chong married his daughter to the crown prince, and [the transfer] then stopped.
units.idiomatic: Chong betrothed his daughter to the crown prince, so the transfer was cancelled.

units.zh: 平吳之後，帝方修太平之化，每延公卿，與論政道。
units.literal: After Wu fell the emperor cultivated Great Peace, hosting ministers to debate policy.
units.idiomatic: Pacifying Wu opened seminars on governance.

units.zh: 楷陳三五之風，次敘漢魏盛衰之跡。
units.literal: Kai traced the Three August Ones and Five Lords, then Han and Wei's rise and fall.
units.idiomatic: He lectured on antiquity's golden ages versus Han-Wei cycles.

units.zh: 帝稱善，坐者嘆服焉。
units.literal: The emperor praised him; listeners sighed admiration.
units.idiomatic: The throne approved and the assembly marveled.

units.zh: 楷子瓚娶楊駿女，然楷素輕駿，與之不平。
units.literal: Kai's son Zan married Yang Jun's daughter though Kai despised Jun.
units.idiomatic: Zan's marriage to Jun's daughter strained Kai's contempt for Jun.

units.zh: 楷有渴利疾，不樂處勢。
units.literal: Kai suffered wasting thirst and loathed heavy responsibility.
units.idiomatic: Diabetes-like thirst made central office unbearable.

units.zh: 王渾為楷請曰：「楷受先帝拔擢之恩，復蒙陛下寵遇，誠竭節之秋也。
units.literal: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.
units.idiomatic: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.

units.zh: 然楷性不競於物，昔為常侍，求出為河內太守；
units.literal: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.
units.idiomatic: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.

units.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
units.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
units.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

source.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
units.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
units.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

translations.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.

units.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
units.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
units.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.
